Why Supply Rates Are Rising Dec. 1 and How to Save Duquesne Light Company

 Understanding the Dec. 1 supply rate increases and what resources are available to customers 
 11/20/26 
 What to Know ​
​ 1. Supply rates will increase on Dec. 1, 2026, for customers on DLC’s default service. ​
​ 2. Supply costs always fluctuate, but the biggest driver over the past two years has been higher energy demand from data centers. ​
​ 3. Resources are available for residential and business customers who need support. 
 Now more than ever, every dollar counts. That’s why we want to explain upcoming changes to your electric bill and where to find helpful resources if needed. 
 What’s Changing 
 As with other electric utilities, Duquesne Light Company (DLC) will adjust default service supply rates on Dec. 1 to reflect the changing price of securing reliable power for our customers. Also known as the “Price to Compare,” these rates will increase from 14.14 cents per kilowatt hour (kWh) to 14.56 cents for most residential customers. 
 This adds approximately $2.49 to a typical monthly bill for residential default-service customers who use an average of 600 kWh of electricity per month. However, your total supply charge depends on your usage and your residential or business rate class. 
 What Supply Charges Pay For 
 Supply charges cover the cost of generation and transmission — that is, the generation of electricity and its transmission from the power facility to DLC’s local distribution network. On Dec. 1, only the generation portion is increasing. 
 Because DLC does not generate electricity, we purchase it for customers through competitive auctions and a mix of contract lengths designed for the lowest cost over time. This process is called default service and is regulated by the Public Utility Commission. Supply costs are passed through to customer bills and adjusted twice a year. DLC does not collect a profit from supply charges. 
 Customers can also choose to shop for their own supplier, which adjusts rates on a different schedule. 
 Learn how to shop smart for a third-party supplier so you don’t overpay. 
 Why Rates Are Increasing 
 Electricity is essential to our lives, but it's also a product influenced by supply and demand. 
 In recent years, energy demand has soared, especially from data centers that power AI technology, both in Pennsylvania and across the PJM regional grid. 
 Aging power generation plants are also retiring faster than replacements can be built, further contributing to a supply-and-demand imbalance and rising prices. 
 How to Get Help ​ 
 We encourage customers to explore all the resources DLC offers, including: 
 Customer Assistance Program (commonly known as “CAP”) 
 Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (commonly known as “LIHEAP”) 
 Hardship grants through Dollar Energy Fund 
 Payment arrangements 
 Budget billing 
 Saving energy may also save money. DLC provides no-cost home energy audits for residential customers to help identify opportunities that might lower your bill and improve home comfort. ​ 
 Not sure where to start? Use DLC's new program finder to explore tailored assistance options.
 Businesses considering energy efficiency upgrades may also qualify for financing, rebates and other incentives . 
 What DLC Is Doing to Address Costs 
 While DLC can’t control broader energy market costs, we can support customers in other ways, including requiring local large data center developers to “pay their own way.” This means that before they can connect to our grid, they — not other customers — must fund necessary planning and construction costs. 
 We're also working at the state and regulatory level to advocate for customer protections, shape new policies and help bring more generation online to meet demand. 
 DLC will continue to explore every path to protect affordable, reliable service while keeping customers informed along the way. 
 Learn more about supply rates and the factors that influence them here .

 About Duquesne Light Company
 For more than 100 years, Duquesne Light Company has provided safe and reliable electric service to communities in southwestern Pennsylvania. Today, our core values of safety, integrity, dependability, equity and community enable us to serve more than 600,000 customers in two counties, including the city of Pittsburgh. We are committed to safely powering our customers’ lives while playing a leading role in our region’s clean energy transition. Our vision is to create a larger-than-light, clean energy future for all by delivering exceptional results today and boldly harnessing opportunities for tomorrow. In doing so, we can ensure a cleaner, healthier and more equitable community for generations to come.
